title: Synthesis: A Personal Thesis
summary: The course exists to produce one thing: a view you can defend. Build a framework, learn to position-size your beliefs, design a sane information diet, sketch three plausible futures, and decide what you owe the people you teach. The module's deliverable is a thesis outline that scaffolds the final 1,500-word personal thesis.
learningOutcomes: Build a framework (a set of questions) for weighing competing narratives without joining a tribe.
Apply Tetlock-style calibration and position sizing to ideas, not just portfolios.
Design a small, deliberate information diet that produces small, slow updates instead of whiplash.
Sketch three plausible 10-year futures with rough probabilities, leading indicators, and a residual for surprise.
Articulate what you owe the people you teach and identify your own most likely failure mode in transmitting uncertain knowledge.
Produce a thesis outline (claim, three sized sub-claims, steel-man, falsifiers) that scaffolds the final project.
capstone: The final 1,500-word personal thesis. See final-project/brief.md. The module's own assignment.md is the pre-writing scaffold for that capstone, not a duplicate of it.
